newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala president sees limited post-war amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala president sees limited post-war amnesty.

text.p: Guatemala President Alvaro Arzu said on Wednesday that government and leftist rebel peace negotiators had reached agreement to grant limited amnesty to participants in the civil war.
The amnesty portion of a peace accord was due to be signed in Madrid on Thursday.

The accord, the final precursor to a definitive peace treaty to be signed Dec. 29, established terms for guerrilla fighters from the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit to return to legal status in Guatemalan society.
The same accord broadly outlined amnesty for some crimes committed during 36 years of brutal civil war, he said.

"Crimes against humanity and cases of kidnapping that have absolutely nothing to do with the armed conflict will be excluded (from the terms of amnesty)," Arzu told reporters as he left to attend a Caribbean and Latin American conference in Miami.
"Those who participated in the armed confrontation in actions that were relevant to it" will receive amnesty, he added.
Arzu said the limited amnesty is in harmony with demands from the international community.
Many Guatemalans have petitioned the government in recent months not to adopt a general amnesty for fighters on either side of the war.

Human rights leaders and opposition politicians have said that unless the limited amnesty is very detailed, it will allow army personnel accused of massacres and political assassinations to avoid justice.
